title: observability-private-inventory.v1
description: The resolved material ADR-0004 keeps out of public Git: what a logical target_id actually points at, which credential a target uses and where that credential is kept, and the identity of the host a promotion reaches. The delivery plan calls a document written against this contract ObserverInventoryV1.  THIS SCHEMA IS PUBLIC AND EVERY DOCUMENT WRITTEN AGAINST IT IS PRIVATE. That is not a contradiction: a schema describes the SHAPE of resolved material, which discloses nothing, while an instance IS the resolved material. Publishing the schema is what lets a reviewer disagree with the split; publishing an instance would be the map ADR-0004 exists to withhold. The only tracked instances are the synthetic .invalid fixtures CI renders against.  Canonical form, for the digest recorded in a promotion receipt and an authorization: UTF-8, `json.dumps(document, indent=2, sort_keys=True)`, NO trailing newline. A reader that adds a trailing newline before hashing reports false drift on a correct inventory, so the form is stated here rather than left to a convention.

document.description: Stable name of this document, recorded in receipts and authorizations beside the digest. A digest identifies bytes; a reader also needs to know which document those bytes were supposed to be.

version.description: Monotonic. Bumped whenever any resolved value changes, so a receipt naming version 4 cannot be satisfied by version 5's bytes even before the digest is compared.

environment.description: Must equal the control plane's `environment`. A production inventory resolved against a staging control plane renders cleanly and points a staging evaluator at production, which is why the equality is a gate rather than a convention.

targets.description: One entry per logical scrape target_id declared in public inventory. Resolution is checked in BOTH directions: an unresolved public target and an unused private binding are each a finding, because a binding nobody reaches is a stale endpoint that no gate would otherwise mention.

endpoint.description: A resolved host, or host:port. Private under ADR-0004 in both halves: the name locates the estate and the port narrows what is listening on it.

openbao_path.description: Where the value lives. Never dereferenced by this repository; recorded so a deployment can place the file. ADR-0004 makes the PATH itself private material, because it describes credential custody layout.

file_name.description: Basename under the control plane's secrets_dir. Private: a basename names which credential a target uses, which is a binding even though it is not a value. PR 6 in this repository's own history exists because a redaction sweep treated a basename as clean.

target_id.description: Must equal the public control-plane document's `host.target_id`.

identity.description: Stable human name of the host. Present so a receipt can record which host was changed.

ssh_alias.description: The alias an operator names when authorizing a promotion. Recorded so the named target and the declared one can be compared; NEVER used to infer a target automatically (AGENTS.md rule 17).

credential.description: Present exactly when the public job declares `authenticated = true`. The public document states the CAPABILITY and the private one supplies the binding, so a disagreement between the two is detectable at resolution — a public claim that a target is authenticated is otherwise unfalsifiable from Git alone.

credential_ref.description: The logical name a public integration cites. Public Git says a receiver has a Telegram integration whose credential is called `oncall`; this document says which token file that is and which chat it reaches.

destination.description: A chat id, mailbox or path. Private: a routing destination identifies a real channel and a real audience, and the delivery plan lists routing destinations as authorization-time material. A URL carrying an embedded key is a credential and belongs in `credential`.
